title: Only Pine Fleet meets the 95% on-time promise, and padding our delivery dates has hidden how far carriers have slipped
subtitle: On-time delivery across the network was 92.1% from January to August. Adding buffer days to the promise made the headline number look better, cost us conversion and left the late tail where it was.
summary: From January to August, 92.1% of parcels arrived by the promised date against a 95% SLA. Only the in-house Pine Fleet (96.4%) met the target; national carriers reached 90.8% and white-glove partners 84.1%. Promise padding introduced in March hid a ~4 pp decline in carrier performance and cost about 1.2% of conversion in the padded lanes, so we recommend removing it lane by lane and moving carriers to scan-based SLAs with penalties.
key_findings: Network on-time vs. promise was 92.1% in Jan–Aug 2026, 2.9 pp below the 95% SLA; Pine Fleet reached 96.4%, national carriers 90.8% and white-glove 84.1%.
In the same ZIPs, Pine Fleet beats national carriers by 3.9–5.8 pp in all six fleet metros.
Against the unpadded transit standard, national-carrier on-time fell from 92.1% to 86.0%; padding hid about 4 pp of that decline.
Padded lanes lost 1.2% of checkout conversion (95% CI 0.4–2.0%), about $3.6M a year in revenue.
Late parcels are 7.9% of deliveries but ~23% of detractors; NPS is +52 when on time and −8 when a parcel is 2+ days late.
